properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, AND IT IS THE ONE HERE THAT MAY SIMPLY BE WRONG. Raised by Anthony asking how CI and regression testing here could be improved, 2026-09-21.

THE PRESSURE THAT MAKES IT WORTH ASKING. The full job has a 60-minute timeout, pays a RocksDB C++ compile, and runs every gate on every push regardless of what changed. A documentation-only PR runs the merge-driver suite, the shared-sessions HTTP suite and the stdio smoke test. As the gate set grows — and it grows with every field report triaged — the cost of a one-line change rises for everyone, and slow feedback is itself a correctness risk because people batch changes to amortise it.

THE MATERIAL TO DO IT WITH ALREADY EXISTS, which is the only reason this is not idle. `impact_of_diff.py` reads a git diff AS A DESIGN CHANGE and reports an unmapped file loudly; the design knows which artifact realizes which capability; `run_ci_gates.py` reads the gate list from the workflow rather than restating it and already takes a filter. Selection would be: diff to artifacts, artifacts to capabilities, capabilities to the Verifications that speak for them, Verifications to gates.

🛑 THE OBJECTION IS THE STRONGEST IN THIS DESIGN, and it is empirical, not theoretical. Running a subset of the gate set and reading it as the whole has happened FOUR TIMES IN ONE DAY and three times as a hand-rebuilt local runner — once 46 tests short, once missing exactly the gate that would have caught the defect, once 17 of 48 with the suite piped through `head -40`. The lesson on the record is a flat sentence: a subset of a gate set is not the gate set. This idea proposes a subset. It cannot stand beside that lesson without the design saying which governs when.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) NOTHING. Always run everything. Costs money and minutes; it is unambiguous, and unambiguous is what the recorded lesson is protecting.
(b) TIER BY COST, NOT BY DIFF — keep running everything, but order gates so the fastest and most-often-red run first and the job fails early. Saves wall-clock on a red build and changes nothing about coverage, so it does not touch the lesson at all. This is the option with no downside that I can see.
(c) SELECTED ON PR PUSHES, FULL ON MERGE TO MAIN AND ALWAYS BEFORE A CUT. The subset is a fast preview; nothing merges without the whole set having run. The failure mode is confusion about which run is authoritative — and note that an unmapped file must expand the selection to everything, never shrink it.
(d) SELECTED EVERYWHERE. This is the one the recorded lesson forbids.

⚠️ If any of these is taken, the selection is itself a gate that must be shown to fail: a selector that matches nothing must run everything, not nothing. That is the same exit-code trap the gate runner's docstring already records.
properties.name: OPEN — should a pull request run a gate set SELECTED from the change's blast radius, when this project's own hardest-won lesson is that a subset of the gate set is not the gate set?
properties.rationale: Recorded open, and recorded WITH its contradiction rather than argued down, because the cost pressure is real and growing while the objection is backed by four measured incidents. Option (b) is separable and carries none of the risk, which suggests the honest outcome may be to take (b) and decline the selection idea outright.
